newsitem.title: BURMA: Guerrillas oppose Burma application for ASEAN.
newsitem.headline: Guerrillas oppose Burma application for ASEAN.

text.p: The leader of Burma's main ethnic guerrillas, the Karen National Union (KNU), on Tuesday urged ASEAN nations not to accept the country as a member of the regional grouping.
General Bo Mya said the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) should not accept Burma as a member because he said it was still run by a "military dictatorship".

"The KNU is strongly opposed to the SLORC's plan to apply for membership of ASEAN and we are appealing to ASEAN nations not to accept a country that is still run by a military dictatorship to be one of its members," the 67-year old KNU leader told reporters at this jungle base in southeastern Burma near the Thai border.
He was referring to Burma's ruling military body, the State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC).
Malaysia's foreign minister Abdullah Badawi said earlier Burma made a formal application for full membership of ASEAN.

The Malaysian national news agency Bernama quoted Abdullah as saying on Tuesday that Burmese Foreign Minister Ohn Gyaw handed over the application last month during a visit to Kuala Lumpur by Burmese junta leader General Than Shwe.
Malaysia is the current chairman of ASEAN, which also groups Indonesia, the Philippines, Brunei, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam. Burma was accepted as an official observer in July.
Bo Mya, whose KNU has been fighting for autonomy from Rangoon, said if ASEAN accepted Burma it would legitimise the SLORC, which has been widely accused of human rights abuses.
"To be a member of ASEAN means democratic countries and world communities recognise the dictatorship and that only will bring more hardship to the Burmese people," he said.
The KNU was formed in 1948 after Burma became independent from Britain and is the last major rebel group left fighting for autonomy from Rangoon.
Despite several rounds of peace talks with the SLORC, an agreement has yet to be made because the military has insisted on unconditional surrender, Bo Mya said.
